questions.q:
Which of the following statements are not correct?

ii. The order of ionization enthalpy of group 13 elements is $\mathrm{B} > \mathrm{Al} > \mathrm{Ga} > \mathrm{In} > \mathrm{Tl}$
iii. Boron trioxide is amphoteric in nature
questions.solution:
The order of atomic radii of group 13 elements varies as:-
$\mathrm{B} < \mathrm{Ga} < \mathrm{Al} < $ In $ < \mathrm{Tl}$
This is due to weak shielding of outermost electrons by $3 \mathrm{ d}$-subshell that causes $\mathrm{Ga}$ to become smaller than $\mathrm{Al}$. Thus, (i) is correct.
The correct order of ionization enthalpy of group 13 elements is :-
$\mathrm{B} > \mathrm{Tl} > \mathrm{Ga} > \mathrm{Al} > $ In
This is due to poor shielding by d-subshells and $\mathrm{f}$-subshells that result in ionization enthalpy being higher for $\mathrm{Tl}$ and $\mathrm{Ga}$.
Thus, statement (ii) is incorrect.
Boron trioxide $\mathrm{B}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ is acidic in nature as it is a nonmetal oxide and dissolves in water to form $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{BO}_3$.
Thus, statement (iii) is incorrect.

iii. $\mathrm{NaBH}_{4}$ is a reducing agent.
questions.solution:
The explanations of given statements are as follows : (i) \($\mathrm{H}}_{3} \mathrm{BO}$}_{3}\) is a monobasic acid because in aqueous solution, it coordinates with a molecule of water to form a hydrated species,
\(\mathrmB^{3+}\) ion pulls the \($\sigma$\)-electron charge of coordinated \($\mathrm{O}$\)-atom towards itself. The coordinated oxygen, in turn, pull the \($\sigma$\)-electrons of \($\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$\) bond of the attached water molecule towards itself. This facilitates the removal of \(\mathrmH^{+}\)ion from the \($\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$\) bond. It can be written as follows: \($\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_$3+$\mathrm{H}}_{2} \mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons\left[\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_4 \Gamma+\mathrmH^{+}\right.\) (ii) The correct formula for borax is \(\mathrm{Na}$}_{2}$\left[\mathrm{~B}}_{4} \mathrm{O}$}_{7}\right] $\cdot$10 $\mathrm{H}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}$\). (iii) \(\mathrm{NaBH}$}_{4}\) is a selective reducing agent for aldehydes, ketones and ester. Thus, statements (i) and (iii) are correct.

- c) Graphite is used as a dry lubricant in machines running at high temperatures. This is correct. Graphite consists of layers that can slide over one another easily, giving it lubricating properties. It is particularly effective at high temperatures where conventional liquid lubricants would vaporize.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion(A): The maximum covalency of Si and Ge is 6 but that of carbon is 4.
Reason (R): Due to the presence of d-orbitals in Si and Ge, both these elements can undergo $\mathrm{sp}^3 \mathrm{ d}^2$ hybridisation and covalency of 6 is possible. Carbon has no d-orbitals in it and hence its covalency is 4.
The correct answer is:
options: (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of $(\mathrm{A})$
(A) and (R) are correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is not the correct explanation of $(\mathrm{A})$
(A) is correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
- Assertion (A): The maximum covalency of Si and Ge is 6, but that of carbon is 4. This is a correct statement. Carbon can form four bonds, achieving a maximum covalency of 4. However, silicon and germanium, being in the same group but a period below carbon, can expand their valence shell to accommodate more than 8 electrons, allowing them to form up to six covalent bonds.
- Reason (R): Due to the presence of d-orbitals in Si and Ge, both these elements can undergo \($\mathrm{sp}^$3 d²\) hybridisation and a covalency of 6 is possible. Carbon has no \(d\)-orbitals in it and hence its covalency is 4. This is a correct explanation. The key difference between carbon and the heavier elements in its group is the availability of empty \($\mathrm{d}$\)-orbitals. These \($\mathrm{d}$\)-orbitals allow silicon and germanium to undergo hybridization beyond \($\mathrm{sp}^$3\) to form molecules like \($\mathrm{SiF}}_{6}^{2-}\) or \( \mathrm{GeCl}$}_{6}^{2-}\), in which the central atom has a coordination number of 6. Carbon lacks these dorbitals, which limits its covalency to 4.

Identify the correct statements from the following
a) Borax gives blue coloured $\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{BO}_2\right)_2$ when heated with $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ salt.
b) The correct formula of Borax is $\mathrm{Na}_2\left[\mathrm{ B}_4 \mathrm{O}_5(\mathrm{OH})_4\right] 8 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
c) Trihalides of boron are Lewis bases.
questions.solution:
- a) Borax gives blue colored \($\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{BO}}_{2}\right)_2\) when heated with \( \mathrm{Co}^{2+}\) salt. This is correct. This is a classic test for metal ions using the borax bead test. When borax is heated, it forms a glassy bead of sodium metaborate and boric anhydride. In the presence of a cobalt salt, cobalt metaborate, \(\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{BO}$}_{2}\right)_2\), is formed, which gives a characteristic blue color.
- b) The correct formula of Borax is \($\mathrm{Na}}_{2}\left[\mathrm{~B}$}_{4} $\mathrm{O}}_{5}( \mathrm{OH})_4\right] \cdot8  \mathrm{H}$}_{2} $\mathrm{O}$\). This is correct. This is the more accurate formula for borax (sodium tetraborate decahydrate), highlighting the presence of a tetraborate anion with a specific structure.
- c) Trihalides of boron are Lewis bases. This is incorrect. Boron trihalides (\(B X_3\)) are Lewis acids because boron has an incomplete octet in these compounds and can accept a pair of electrons.
Statements \(\mathbf{a}\) and \(\mathbf{b}\) are correct.
